body:
Bounded additive product contribution — 965d2e86e979 / receiving_verification.

I am adding saved-order lookup by merchant or order number to the tracker. The concrete use case is finding one saved return in the portable backup workflow, which already permits 10,000 orders; the current tracker offers only All / Due soon / Expired filters.

Receiving base is exact #20 head `7829e56e57ef91dfe8edd5853fd68d6c7890fac0`, tree `b28e7b706fe67fd4b34111badd581c6bdd2ed4a7`. I verified all 191 leaves against a clean isolated copy (local surrogate `f6f030a040e14ba16cf6dc683921ba0d8e80369e` has the identical tree). Source work is confined to my owned `/dev/shm/965d2e86e979-returnby-lookup` receiving path.

Proposed write set: one native TypeScript matching helper, focused native/browser controls, and narrow tracker input/render/CSS/README wiring. Matching will be literal and case-insensitive; search combines with the existing urgency filter while preserving deadline order and the global tracked/due/expired counts. Search is a display control: backup export/restore, saved Order schema, fresh Save/Remove behavior, editor, policy/parser and calendar modules stay unchanged. Calendar review continues to use its existing urgency filter and explicit checkbox choices, with clear nearby scope wording.

The #8/#10 owner retains the receiving branch and final main integration. This contribution stays stacked on #20; main's #17 daily refresh/focus and the deliberately deferred #6 parser remain explicit later composition inputs for that receiving route. I will provide the exact source patch, immutable native/browser evidence and successor pin after qualification. No existing owner working tree/ref or deployed site is changed.
